title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1969-06-08

ai_review.summary: Stunning soundboard stereo mix captures an iconic 1969 Fillmore West set highlighted by a psychedelic Lovelight > The Things I Used To Do > Who's Lovin' You Tonight run.
ai_review.review: This recording delivers high‑quality, crisp stereo soundboard audio that lets the 1969 Fillmore West performance shine.  The show is repeatedly described as a peak psychedelic excursion, with Phil Lesh’s dose‑induced bass frenzy and a standout Lovelight sequence anchoring an otherwise superb setlist.  No serious technical flaws are noted, making it both a listening pleasure and a historic snapshot.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews (5‑star and 4‑star) praise both the performance and the recording, with only one outlier. Weighted averaging of show (≈3.8) and recording quality (≈4.5) yields a strong overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: High‑quality stereo audio with an excellent mix; reviewers call it crisp, clear, and great for a '69 era recording. No dropouts or balance issues mentioned.

standout_songs: Lovelight > The Things I Used To Do > Who's Lovin' You Tonight
He Was a Friend of Mine > China Cat Sunflower > New Potato Caboose
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set is praised as an exemplary excursion, comparable to the 5/2/70 gold‑standard show. Strong first‑set run leads into a centerpiece second‑set sequence that showcases the group's collective improvisational peak.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Reviewers evoke vivid psychedelic imagery centered on Jerry’s guitar, describing his playing as part of a “bridge of light” and noting perfect tone in other comments.
band_member_comments.Phil: Multiple reviewers highlight Phil Lesh’s LSD‑enhanced bass performance—he didn’t recognize his own instrument at first, calling it the peak of psychedelic music creation for him.
